label: Subtraction vocabulary: concrete presence, finitely many, could fail to exist, no newcomer
term: subtraction (concrete presence, possible failure to exist, subtraction without newcomer)
definition: On the route's profile m (frame m.ontic.frame, rigid candidates, world-relative existence m.ontic.ExistsAt, world-independent concreteness m.concrete): ConcretePresence m x v holds when x is concrete and exists at v. PossiblyFinitelyManyConcrete m w (S1): some world v accessible from w has all its concrete objects in one finite list. EachConcreteCouldFailAt m v (S2 at v): every concrete object existing at v is absent at some world accessible from v; ...Throughout m w asks this at every world accessible from w. NoNewcomer m v u: every concrete object existing at u exists at v. SubtractableAt m v (S3, conditional subtraction): every concrete object x existing at v that is absent at some world accessible from v is absent at some world u accessible from v with NoNewcomer m v u; NonNecessitationAt is the unconditional (literal) form, which equals S2 plus SubtractableAt. PossiblyNoConcrete m w: the stage-one JointAbsence of the concrete-presence predicate, some world accessible from w with no concrete object. NotEachConcreteCouldFailAt is the negation of S2 at w. The analyst formulation of Lowe's reply uses NecessaryAbstractumAt (a non-concrete candidate existing at every world accessible from w) and AbstractaNeedConcretaThroughout (at every accessible world where a non-concrete candidate exists, some concrete object also exists: co-existence only, not grounding or dependence for being).
note: Analyst formulation, attribution deferred: Baldwin 1996, Rodriguez-Pereyra 1997 and 2002, Efird and Stoneham 2005 and Lowe 1998 and 2002 are navigation only, no source claim. Possibility is accessibility in the route's frame; nothing here asserts that the frame's worlds are the metaphysically possible worlds. 'Could fail to exist' is the frame's diamond of non-existence. The statements of this batch tag it with the frame carrier sense NECESSARY_11 (f8948e28: worlds, accessibility, truth at a world), the sense of the route frame's transitivity premise, because the subtraction argument uses only possibility over the frame. Its dual is the route's NecessaryAt (NECESSARY_2 box-existence); the passage between the two is the existing bridge statement STMT-NECESSARY-CONCRETE-AT, declared in sense_bridges where an argument uses it, and the premise-free controls relate the two as a sense-mixing control. With excluded middle, S2 at w is with excluded middle exactly the denial of STMT-NECESSARY-CONCRETE-AT at w (controls). Finiteness is covering by a List because the family is zero-axiom and does not import Mathlib; covering by a finite list is the standard characterization of Set.Finite. S3 realizes the absence jointly at one world: pairwise absence (recombination) does not suffice (controls, pair model). Concreteness is the profile's parameter m.concrete (INHABITED_CONCRETE_WORLD_2 usage), whose intended criterion in the corpus is CONCRETE_AND_ABSTRACT_6, esse in re (DISAMB-CONCRETE-ABSTRACT-CRITERIA). The subtraction literature uses a spatiotemporal or causal criterion (CONCRETE_AND_ABSTRACT_7, CONCRETE_AND_ABSTRACT_5). Identifying its 'concrete' with m.concrete is a reading choice, not a bridge: every theorem holds for any supplied predicate, and the dialectical findings hold for whichever criterion fixes m.concrete on both sides. The analyst formulation of Lowe's reply does not formalize any further explanatory premise of Lowe's own modal argument.
